name: Per-Quest Mechanics
content:
Bane & Boon

The dice tell a story. They do so in the moment as rolls determine the outcomes of specific actions, but in Renaissance, they also tug at the threads of fate over time. This is represented by BANE & BOON.

As players roll skill checks and other checks requiring a feat die (d12), they will occasionally produce a result of Sol 🌞 or Morte 💀. Each Sol 🌞 moves the party one notch toward BOON. Each Morte 💀 moves the party one notch toward BANE.

The party starts in a neutral state at the beginning of each quest, in the center of the scale. The number of notches between neutral and BANE/BOON is equal to the number of player characters in the party, minus one. So a party with four player characters would have a BANE/BOON scale like this:

BANE ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- || ----- | ----- | ----- | ----- BOON

Only skill checks for player characters effect BANE & BOON. Rolls made by NPCs do not count.

When the party reaches BANE, the GM takes a hard move: they dictate something that has immediate, irrevocable consequences. The GM is encouraged not to hold back. A BANE should be very, very bad.

When the party reaches BOON, the players propose their own "hard move," though in this case it's a good thing that has immediate, irrevocable consequences. The GM has full discretion in whether to accept or reject the players' proposal, but is encouraged to be generous. They players can also ask the GM to dictate the BOON. Either way, don't hold back - a BOON should be an exceptional moment of triumph or good fortune.

The party's position on the BANE/BOON scale at the end of the quest has no effect, and they start back at neutral at the beginning of the next quest. We do not track BANE/BOON outside of the Quest phase of the game.

The GM may track BANE/BOON themselves or delegate the duty to a player. Either way, the current status of the BANE/BOON scale is always public information.

Compagnia

COMPAGNIA are points that represent the camaraderie among the party members during a Quest. It is a shared resource. The party starts each Quest with a total Compagnia equal to the number of party members.

During the quest, any time a character rolls a failure on a skill check, any player may propose using Compagnia to add an additional success die (d6) to the roll before determining success or failure.

All players must agree in order for Compagnia to be used. This is an above-the-table discussion, meaning it's the players discussing the significance of the moment, not the characters.

However, once the decision to use Compagnia has been made, take a moment to weave it into the narrative. What is it about this party in particular that motivates or enables the active character to push themself beyond their normal limits?

If any Compagnia remains at the end of the quest, it may be used to benefit the characters who completed the quest, as outlined in the Rest & Recovery section. Otherwise, the Compagnia is forfeited.
